question.text: Mr. Rajesh Menon, Fund Manager at Lotus Ventures Category II AIF, is briefing a new analyst on how Venture Capital screening differs from Angel-stage screening. Which metric is PRIMARILY used by VCs (and not by angels, who mainly look at the founding team) to validate that revenue generation is consistent and sustainable in an investee start-up?

answer.text: Customer Acquisition Cost to Customer Lifetime Value ratio based on projected demand
Total Addressable Market derived from industry reports
Monthly Run Rate (MRR) or Annual Run Rate (ARR) of the investee company
Net Promoter Score measured on early beta users

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.1.2 (Venture Capital Investments), VC investors target revenue-generating companies and specifically use Monthly Run Rate (MRR) and Annual Run Rate (ARR) to gauge consistency and sustainability of revenues. Angels, by contrast, invest at the idea stage and bet on the founding team, not on ARR. The Trap: CAC/CLV is used by both angels and VCs but is not the specific revenue-sustainability metric cited. TAM is a market-size concept, not a revenue metric. NPS is a customer-satisfaction indicator, not a cash-flow validation metric VCs rely on. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) covers VC in distributor framing; XIX-C tests the Manager's diligence checklist — MRR/ARR, Cash Burn, CAC/CLV, TAM/SAM/SOM funnel. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before signing an NDA with a Series A target, demand last 12 months of revenue in MRR format — smoothed, not lumpy. Founders tempted to show one big-order quarter instead of consistent ARR are a red flag.
